transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-12-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Marshall (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood Product), Jordan Lee (Citrine - Head of Search), Priya Nair (Citrine ML Eng), Samir Patel (Citrine InfoSec), Anya Volk (Citrine PM), Mo (Citrine SWE)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + rerank endpoints for Citrine Commerce's product search use case. Discussed expected throughput, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and pilot steps. Agreed to run a two-week pilot with a small product catalog and benchmark script.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, /embeddings and /rerank flow, Redwood Console demo, Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, security docs, pilot scope and success metrics.

--- Transcript ---
[15:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan, I'm the AE on this account and with me is Maya who will do the demo. Luis is here for product questions.
[15:12] Jordan (Customer): Hi thanks, appreciate you folks. We just want to see the hosted api flow for embeddings and how we could do reranking, and figure out costs and security.
[15:20] Ethan: Perfect. Quick qual: Jordan, what are you running now? What's the stack?
[15:25] Jordan: Right now we've got a hybrid. We use Postgres for metadata, the vectors go into Pinecone for retrieval, then we do a small in-house ranker for product matching. We're exploring replacing the local ranker with a small rerank model endpoint. Latency target is sub 120 ms for the first-byte on search for our top tier. Cost target is to not blow past current infra spend, so... cost sensitive.
[15:48] Maya (Redwood SE): Cool. That's a common pattern. We'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint, and the /rerank endpoint which does a pre-computed retrieval plus a neural rerank stage. There are a few knobs we'll call out for latency vs cost: batching, prefix caching (k v cache), and quantized model variants.
[16:05] Priya (Customer): Question: how do you do batching with the hosted api? We have bursty traffic, like Black Friday spikes.
[16:12] Maya: Right. Hosted supports continuous batching in the runtime; you can configure the max latency window. For burst, you can use Redwood Dedicated or burst capacity options. For hosted, we also have smart routing with fallback model variants to keep latency bounded if a GPU pool is saturated.
[16:29] Samir (InfoSec): From security: do you retain query content or embeddings? We need to understand retention policies and KMS options.
[16:36] Luis (Redwood Product): We have configurable retention. Hosted default is short retention for logs and aggregated telemetry; you can opt-in for longer retention for debugging. For private keying, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via our Private offering, and for hosted we do envelope encryption with our keys — we can discuss Bring Your Own Key in the Private plan.
[16:55] Jordan: Is SOC 2 a yes?
[16:57] Ethan: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We'll send the attestation and security pack after.
[17:05] Anya (PM): For the rerank model, can we bring our own model checkpoints? We want to test a fine-tuned reranker.
[17:11] Maya: Hosted supports model variants in the catalog; we can onboard a custom model but that typically goes through an onboarding process — more straightforward on Dedicated or Private. For hosted pilot, we recommend using a Redwood-verified rerank model to get stable perf, then migrate to custom weights when ready.
[17:30] Mo (SWE): Any advice on vector db compatibility? We use Pinecone currently, will switching to Redwood require changing pipeline?
[17:36] Maya: Not really. Retrieval can stay in Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, or your internal vector store. The flow is: retrieve top-K ids from your vector db, call /rerank with the candidate set and the query embeddings or raw query; rerank returns re-score and you display. We show an example script in the console.
[17:54] Ethan: We'll demo that flow now — embeddings, retrieval, then /rerank. Maya, take it away.
[17:59] Maya: Sure. Sharing my screen... ok, console.redwood.ai... excuse the slowness.
[18:10] Maya: First, the embeddings endpoint. You can POST to /v1/embeddings with the text payload, and we return a 1536-d vector (example). In the console you can send sample payloads, see token counts, and export the vector. There's also an embeddings-batch endpoint for bulk indexing.
[18:33] Priya: Is the vector dimension fixed? We have workflows with different dims.
[18:36] Maya: We support multiple dims depending on model. Most curated models are 1536 or 1024. If you need a custom dim you'd use your fine-tuned model; that is a separate onboarding.
[18:49] [18:50] Maya: Now rerank. The endpoint accepts candidates as an ordered list and returns scores. We can do cross-encoder style reranking or a lightweight feed-forward re-ranker depending on latency needs. For product search we often recommend a lightweight reranker for sub-120ms SLAs.
[19:12] Jordan: Can rerank also take metadata like price or stock to bias results?
[19:16] Maya: Yes, you can pass structured metadata — we have structured inputs and function-like calls. You can incorporate signal features into the reranker; the console demo shows a feature-augmentation flow.
[19:33] [19:34] Maya: Quick note on cost: reranking all 100 candidates is expensive. Typical pattern is retrieve 50-100 candidates, do a cheap filter, then rerank top 10. Redwood Optimize provides cost estimates and recommends candidate sizes and quantization levels to balance accuracy and spend.
[19:58] Jordan: How do you measure quality? We have in-house metrics like MRR and click-through.
[20:03] Luis: We integrate evaluation sets in the Console. You can upload a small test set and run A/B experiments. Optimize will flag regressions and provide suggestions for quantization or model swaps.
[20:18] Ethan: Let's talk throughput. What's your average qps and p95 latency target?
[20:23] Jordan: Currently ~70 qps on read searches during peak, p95 ~180ms, looking to get p95 under 120ms for top tier.
[20:31] Maya: For hosted, sub-120 p95 is achievable with the lightweight reranker model plus batching and prefix/K V cache. We'll provide a recommended config. If you need strict SLOs at scale, Dedicated is better.
[20:50] Priya: Any limits on tokens or rate limits?
[20:54] Ethan: Hosted has per-account rate limits configurable by plan; we'll share defaults. For pilot we can increase quotas.
[21:00] Samir: On compliance, can we get logs for audit? We need user-level access logs and redaction support.
[21:06] Luis: Yes, audit logs and RBAC are supported. For hosted, logs are retained per plan; Private gives you full control. We also support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[21:25] [21:26] Jordan: Any concerns around data residency in EU?
[21:29] Ethan: We have cloud regions in EU and can route traffic to EU-hosted model pools. For strict residency, Private/VPC is the recommended path.
[21:40] Maya: Ok demo part two: live request. I'm sending a sample query to /v1/embeddings... response back in 120 ms. Vector returned. Now we simulate a retrieval from Pinecone and call /v1/rerank with 12 candidates — request returns in 95 ms. You can see score deltas and the console visualization of reranked order.
[22:05] Mo: Nice. The UI shows token-level cost?
[22:08] Maya: Yes, per-request token breakdown and cost estimate. The Console has per-route dashboards and tracing hooks so you can tie token spend to a product or route.
[22:20] Anya: For the pilot, what's a minimal dataset? We have about 500k products but can run with a slice.
[22:25] Maya: Recommend 10k-50k products with a 1k query eval set. That gets you useful signals while keeping pilot cost reasonable.
[22:34] Jordan: Ok timeline: we want results within the first two weeks. We can provide an eval set and priors.
[22:39] Ethan: Great. We'll propose a two-week pilot: week 1 index + baseline runs, week 2 tuning + reranking and a final report.
[22:48] [23:00] Samir: We'll send a list of infosec questions. On encryption: do you support BYOK for hosted?
[23:06] Luis: For hosted, we do envelope encryption with our keys; BYOK is available on Private. We can also provide attestation for key handling on hosted if that's helpful.
[23:18] Priya: Any mention of model drift monitoring? We want to ensure rerank quality doesn't slowly degrade.
[23:23] Luis: Console has quality monitoring. You upload a probe set; Optimize will run periodic evals and alert on regression.
[23:33] [23:35] Maya: One caveat: if you push a custom model to hosted, performance can vary; we can run a small benchmark on our infra. We'll include that benchmark script.
[23:47] Jordan: Competitor question — we use Pinecone now, why choose Redwood?
[23:51] Ethan: Redwood is inference-first: we provide both the embeddings and the rerank with a unified operational surface. Cost controls like automatic batching, prefix caching and quantization recommendations can reduce per-query spend vs homegrown rerankers. Also first-class observability and rollouts.
[24:10] Anya: Pricing ballpark?
[24:13] Ethan: For a pilot, we'll propose a fixed pilot fee plus usage for embeddings and rerank. For production, hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is flat reserved for large QPS. I'll send detailed tiers.
[24:29] Priya: A quick nit: you referenced "K V cache" earlier — can you explain that?
[24:33] Maya: Sure — it's our KV cache for key-value attention caches to speed up autoregressive workloads. For rerank it's less relevant, but for chat/LM-heavy use it matters.
[24:45] Jordan: Back to rerank: can we run A/B between our in-house ranker and Redwood rerank?
[24:49] Maya: Absolutely. Console supports canary and A/B rollouts with traffic splits and automatic fallback. You can run both and measure CTR/MRR.
[25:02] [25:15] Maya: Demo wrap-up: shared examples, benchmark notebook link (https://redwood.ai/pilot-notebook) and a small colab with retrieval->rerank script.
[25:30] Ethan: Ok let's do a quick Q&A and then recap next steps.
[25:37] Jordan: Two quick qu's: latency on cold start for hosted, and how do you handle schema changes in metadata?
[25:44] Maya: Cold start for a warmed model pool is low; for a model not recently used you can see a 200-400 ms bump. We have warm pools for top customers. Metadata schema: rerank input is flexible and we version the API — small changes are supported without breaking.
[26:05] Priya: If we choose hosted pilot, who owns the onboarding?
[26:09] Ethan: We'll assign a solutions engineer (Maya is the SE lead) and an onboarding PM. For pilots we do a kickoff and weekly check-ins.
[26:20] Samir: One compliance last thing: do you provide contractual SLAs for hosted?
[26:25] Luis: Hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated has contractual SLAs with uptime and latency targets. For the pilot we'll agree on success metrics.
[26:38] [26:50] Jordan: Alright that's a lot. Any other blockers?
[26:54] Anya: I have a follow-up about personalization signals integration; we'll send examples.
[26:58] Ethan: Great. Recap of next steps: send pilot pricing and template, share benchmark script and console recording, Samir to send security Qs, schedule kickoff week of Jan 8.
[27:10] [27:30] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll also include a short doc on recommended candidate sizes and quantization levels.
[27:40] Jordan: Thanks, that was useful.
[27:45] Ethan: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email and slack.
